proposal.title: Known URLs answered from the recipe
proposal.author: Giovanni Porcari

problem.p: External clients read some documents at fixed paths of a site. Examples: /.well-known/security.txt (RFC 9116), /robots.txt, /.well-known/apple-app-site-association (iOS universal links), /.well-known/assetlinks.json (Android app links).

The content of these documents depends on the deployment, not on the code: a contact address, the crawler rules, the identifiers of a mobile app. The same application code runs on sites that need different values.

In kajenn an application serves a /.well-known/ document only by declaring it in its code. A fixed path outside /.well-known/, such as /robots.txt, has no mechanism of its own. A site cannot declare these documents in its recipe.
genropy legacy answers these four documents from the instance configuration, with no code per site.

section.title: kajenn today: routing
section.fact: A first path segment starting with a dot gets 404 from the server demux and reaches no application. The one exception is .well-known followed by a name in well_known_applications: the request goes to that application with its path rebuilt as /_well_known/<name>/<rest>.
A RoutedApplication declares its documents as the children of a _well_known branch of its router. well_known_names returns those children. BaseApplication.well_known_names returns ().
register_application first sets app.server = self, then calls index_well_known(app, app.well_known_names). The names are read once, at that moment.
index_well_known keeps one index name → application. A name declared by two applications belongs to the last registered.
An external application presents its names in meta["well_known"] when its process joins the KajennBus. The server re-indexes them.
A path without a leading dot, /robots.txt and /favicon.ico included, is demuxed like any other path: it reaches the application mounted on that first segment, else the root application, else 404.
section.p: The proposal channels-meta-and-server-gui moves the branch _well_known to _meta/well_known. The public path /.well-known/ does not change. This proposal holds for both locations.

section.title: kajenn today: the _server application and its recipe words
section.fact: The server always mounts a ServerApplication under _server when no declared application has that code.

ServerApplicationGrammar holds the recipe words of _server. The recipe writes them under applications.application(app_class=ServerApplication, code="_server"): today login(...) and oidc().provider(...). The words live in the application that owns the function, not in the site dialect.

The server setter of ServerApplication calls read_declared_login_surface, which reads the login and oidc nodes of the recipe. The setter runs inside register_application, before the well-known names are indexed.
attach_section asks extensions to register their sections during startup, after the application is registered. A _well_known child added at that time is not in the index.

section.title: kajenn today: static files and the proxy
section.fact: SiteHome.static names a folder for favicon, robots and sitemap. No code under src/ serves that folder.
The default storage mount home: is the space the site keeps its own things in, statics included. It is anchored on the folder of the site card.
The local HTTPS deployment puts Caddy in front of kajenn with reverse_proxy kajenn:8080. A reverse proxy can answer a fixed path before kajenn sees the request.

section.title: genropy legacy
section.fact: At startup the site reads alias_url from the __call__ of every webtool found by find_webtools(). It builds webtools_static_routes, a dict absolute path → webtool name.
_dispatcher looks up request.path in that dict before every other rule. On a match it serves the webtool through serve_tool(['_tools', <name>]). The match is on the exact whole path.
A webtool declares its path with @metadata(alias_url=...) on __call__. The path may be outside /.well-known/: RobotsTxt uses /robots.txt.

row.cell: One Field: value line per child
User-agent blocks with their rules, plus global lines
JSON applinks and webcredentials, with excluded paths
JSON with package name and certificate fingerprints

section.fact: A document whose configuration is missing raises an exception at request time.

list.item: The recipe declares the documents the site answers at fixed paths. Each declaration carries the data of the document, not its text.
kajenn generates the body from that data, with the media type the standard requires. No application code is needed.
The first set is the legacy one: security.txt, robots.txt, apple-app-site-association, assetlinks.json.
A document not declared in the recipe does not exist: its path follows today's rules (404 under /.well-known/, normal demux elsewhere). There is no runtime exception for a missing configuration.
Wrong data is refused at boot, not at request time.
Applications keep declaring their own /.well-known/ documents in code, as today.

section.title: Recipe words on the _server application
section.p: The declarations are words of ServerApplicationGrammar, written under the _server application element like login and oidc. No site-level element is added.

ServerApplication reads them in its server setter, where it already reads login and oidc, and builds the children of its _well_known branch there. The setter runs before register_application indexes the names, so /.well-known/<name> reaches _server through the existing index. demux_hidden does not change.
Decision d-owner compares this with the alternatives. A root path such as /robots.txt has no existing mechanism: decision d-root covers it.

section.title: Example recipe shape
section.p: The element names below do not exist in the code. They are placeholders until the decisions below are taken.
section.code: server_app = applications.application(app_class=ServerApplication, code="_server") server_app.security_txt(contact="mailto:security@acme.example", expires="2027-11-01T00:00:00Z") server_app.robots_txt(rules=[{"user_agent": "*", "disallow": ["/_server/"]}]) server_app.ios_app(team_id="ABCDE12345", bundle_id="example.acme.app", excluded_paths=["/_server/*"]) server_app.android_app(package_name="example.acme.app", fingerprints=["AA:BB:..."])

decision.question: Which documents are in the first cut?

option.title: The four legacy documents
option.p: Pro: parity with genropy legacy; every format is already known. Con: none known.

option.title: The legacy four plus openid-configuration, change-password and sitemap.xml
option.p: Pro: covers more probes. Con: code for documents no site asks for today.

decision.question: Which component answers the recipe documents?

option.title: ServerApplication, from its own recipe words
option.p: Pro: _server is always mounted; its grammar already holds recipe words; the branch is built before indexing, so neither the demux nor the index changes. Con: _server gains a role that is not administration.

option.title: The server demux, before the application index
option.p: Pro: works with no application at all. Con: the demux generates content, which today it never does; the words would go in the site dialect.

option.title: An application the site declares in the recipe
option.p: Pro: explicit; uses only today's mechanism. Con: every site that wants one document must add an application.

option.title: The reverse proxy (Caddy, Traefik)
option.p: Pro: no kajenn code. Con: the data lives outside the recipe; every deployment writes it again in its proxy syntax; a site without a proxy has nothing.

decision.question: How is a root path outside /.well-known/ (/robots.txt) answered?

option.title: An exact-path index in the demux, checked before the mount lookup
option.p: Pro: same rule as legacy; one dict lookup. Con: a site path shadows a mount with the same first segment.

option.title: Left to the root application, as today
option.p: Pro: no change. Con: a site with no root application cannot answer /robots.txt.

option.title: Left to the reverse proxy
option.p: Pro: no kajenn code. Con: same as d-owner-proxy; robots.txt data and /.well-known/ data end up in two places.

option.title: Only /.well-known/ documents are in scope
option.p: Pro: smallest change. Con: robots.txt, part of the legacy set, is left out.

decision.question: What happens when an application declares a name the recipe also declares?

option.title: Boot fails with FatalBootError
option.p: Pro: no silent winner. Con: an external application that joins later cannot be refused at boot.

option.title: The recipe wins
option.p: Pro: the site has the last word over application code. Con: changes today's rule (the last registered wins).

option.title: Today's rule: the last registered wins
option.p: Pro: no new rule. Con: the result depends on registration order.

decision.question: Are files kept by the site (favicon.ico, sitemap.xml) also served at fixed paths?

option.title: No, out of this proposal
option.p: Pro: keeps generated documents and files apart. Con: SiteHome.static stays a folder nobody serves.

option.title: Yes, read through the home: storage mount
option.p: Pro: uses the mount that already holds the site's statics; the same code works on a non-local backend. Con: depends on d-root.

list.item: ServerApplicationGrammar gains one element per document type. The site dialect does not change.
No new dependency: every format is plain text or JSON.
A genropy site moved to kajenn writes the same data in the recipe instead of wku.* and mobile_app.*.

A _well_known child added to _server after registration, for example by an extension through attach_section, is not indexed. Serving it needs a new call to index_well_known. This proposal does not add that call.
With d-root-exact, the demux gains one lookup before the mount lookup.
